newsitem.title: USA: CPC to take pre-tax $328 mln charge in Q2.
newsitem.headline: CPC to take pre-tax $328 mln charge in Q2.

text.p: CPC International Inc said Thursday it will take two pre-tax charges totalling $328 million in the second quarter.
The food company said it will take a pre-tax charge of $86 million -- $65 million after tax or $0.45 a common share -- related to the cost of spinning off its corn refining operations.
It said it will also take a pre tax charge of $242 million -- $155 million after tax or $1.08 a share -- in connection with the restructuring of its packaged foods operation.

It said the restructuring is expected to result in savings that will reach $60 million in 1998 and more than $90 million in 1999 and thereafter. That, it said, will add substantially to its future operating income.
CPC said that, as previously announced, it expects to spin off its global corn refining operations by the end of the year.
It said that about 50 percent of the restructuring charge relates to its worldwide consumer foods business, 35 percent for its baking business and 15 percent for cuts in corporate overhead.
The consumer foods business restructuring affects European and North American operations and includes the sale of some non-core businesses and potential plant closings, it said.
It also involves reorganization of administrative functions and the previously announced transfer of Mueller's pasta production to an outside manufacturer, it said.
C.R. Shoemate, chairman and chief executive officer, said the restructuring "further indicates our commitmenet to achieve rapid growth in our global packaged foods business."
CPC, with sales of $9.8 billion in 1996, carries brands that include Hellman's, Best Foods, Mazola, Skippy and Entenmann's.
